📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, well, in the Season 1 finale of Netflix's The Body, that's exactly what you get.
  • Recent findings suggest that those two words fan the flames of the religious fervor that's been building around Grace and her supposed miracles, and the season ends with a horde of people laying hands on her while she smiles up at her ceiling.
  • Throughout The Body, the series has constantly asked viewers whether they're skeptics or true believers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, well, in the Season 1 finale of Netflix's The Body, that's exactly what you get. That's because, after seven episodes spent in a deep coma following the Halloween party from hell, St. Mark's Catholic High School student Grace (Sofia Wylie) finally wakes up. When she does, she has one bombshell to drop: "I'm God.".

Recent findings suggest that those two words fan the flames of the religious fervor that's been building around Grace and her supposed miracles, and the season ends with a horde of people laying hands on her while she smiles up at her ceiling. But what is the truth behind Grace's miraculous recovery, and what will happen now that she's awake? Let's dive in.

Throughout The Body, the series has constantly asked viewers whether they're skeptics or true believers. Did Grace fall into a coma because of a bad reaction to ecstasy, or did the St. Mark's Lions dance team truly sacrifice her soul to the Devil to secure a win at Regionals? Has Grace been performing saintly miracles, or have all the strange goings-on in her community merely been coincidences (or something darker)?

It has been revealed that the Body has threaded the needle skillfully enough that you could make arguments for both sides. Yes, Grace's blood tests came back clean, suggesting some unknown, perhaps even supernatural, reason for her coma. Yet in the finale, we find out that the doctors never tested her for ecstasy, as it's not part of the standard blood panel, meaning those clean blood tests are missing a huge part of the story.

Industry observers note that and yes, Maddie's (Shirley Chen) and Catherine's (Louisa Krause) recoveries both seem like miracles. But could Maddie's ankle not have been completely healed after all, as she claimed? One of the Lions recalls seeing her limp before the Star Quality competition, although that in itself could have been a false memory. Elsewhere, Catherine's improved condition could have come as a result of a lack of methamphetamine use after her stay in the hospital and her daughter Lisbeth (Geena Meszaros) getting rid of her stashes at home. Coach Shauna's (Gabby Windey) baby's premature birth and total convalescence is similarly miraculous, with even doctors saying the child should have died. But did Grace really come to Shauna in labor to save her baby, or was the baby's survival a happy accident or a miracle of science?

According to recent reports, everything involving the visions is hearsay as well, aside from the frightening warnings Anya (Kristina Bogic) receives. Are people in and around St. Mark's truly experiencing these visitations, or are they, like Elise (Sara Boustany) and some other members of the Lions, making them up? More importantly, if the visitations are real, are they actually holy in nature? Or are they hellish byproducts of the Lions' playful sacrifice of Grace to the Devil?

However you view these prior happenings will impact how you view Grace's waking. Maybe she's just loopy after a prolonged coma, and "I'm God" is her muddled brain repeating what she's heard from people around her. Maybe she truly is a manifestation of God, as much of St. Mark's Church believes, and all the miracles are totally real. Or maybe she's possessed by the Devil, as Catherine is convinced, and she's chosen now as a moment to wake up and begin bringing about the end of days.

In a recent development, the clearest clue to supernatural involvement in Grace's waking comes down to the specific timing of it. It happens right after Anya arrives at Grace's house and confesses her wrongdoings to Father Franklin (Nnamdi Asomugha), telling him, "I'm so sorry that I traded my soul, and I just want it back.".

As Anya utters those words, Grace's eyes flutter open in her bedroom. That sequence of events could be a coincidence, as could so many of The Body's plot points. But it could also point to an otherworldly trade. In finally confessing and asking for her soul back, Anya may have released whatever supernatural hold is right now on Grace and been saved from her own guilt. Of course, that comes with its own set of complications: What may be asked of her in return for being "saved"? And who's asking? Is God truly inhabiting Grace, as she claims, or has the Devil been lurking within her this whole time, even managing to survive Father Franklin's exorcism?

Another element of Grace's miraculous waking is the presence of a moth, which flies down from her ceiling light to rest on her forehead moments before Grace opens her eyes. A small pink moth drawing features in the corners of the finale's opening title cards, so it's clearly of some significance. But what?

Like butterflies, moths are often symbols of transformation. Transformation does track with Grace in the finale, as she transforms back to her conscious state. She may also have transformed into a saint or a Satanic agent — could the moth clue us into which?

On the one hand, moths are nocturnal creatures, suggesting darkness, and therefore a transformation of a more devilish bent. But at the same time, moths are attracted to light. Could the moth have left the literal light on Grace's ceiling and flown towards the metaphorical light emanating from her now-saintly being?

According to recent reports, as with most things in The Body, the answer is ambiguous and up for interpretation. The show is designed to keep you guessing and questioning the evidence before you. Is Grace's smile at the end innocent, or devious? Will you be taken in by her, or will you be wary of false prophets?

If The Body gets a second season, there are so many paths to explore. Obviously, there's the impact of Grace's return, and the examination of whether she's possessed by the Devil or anointed by God. There's also the fallout from Anya's confession, which impacts her relationships with Elise and Steven (Orlando Norman). And of course, there's the Lions' path to Nationals, which I'm sure will go just as smoothly as their path to Regionals.

According to recent reports, but perhaps most fascinating of all is what will happen after Lisbeth tells the Lions that she personally resurrected Grace. Will her attempt to raise her status with the team set up a battle of miracles between her and Grace? Or will she be cast aside now that Grace has returned? There's a lot of potential for more high drama going forward, drama that's juicier than even the Lions' most stylish Juicy Couture.

As of now, Netflix has yet to renew The Body for a second season.

  • When you search 'The Hunger Games', 'Sunrise on the Reaping', or 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' on Google, you'll find a symbol depicting a snake entwined with a mockingjay bird (or the 'flint striker' as hardcore fans know it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The anticipation for the next installment of The Hunger Games saga has never been this fierce (I should know; I've had my IMAX screening tickets booked for weeks), and it seems Google is holding its own celebrations ahead of the Second Quarter Quell.

Sources indicate that if there's one thing Google is great at, it's the fun Easter eggs in its web and mobile search engines, especially when it comes to huge movie introduces. The company did one for Wicked (2024), making your search results 'defy gravity', but its latest one is all about the upcoming The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping movie, which arrives in cinemas on November 20.

When you search 'The Hunger Games', 'Sunrise on the Reaping', or 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' on Google, you'll find a symbol depicting a snake entwined with a mockingjay bird (or the 'flint striker' as hardcore fans know it). Click on it, and you'll be transported down an interactive rabbit hole that tests your knowledge of all things from the world of Panem.

Basically, the feature is a 12-step quest that leads you through a series of questions intertwined with interactive games you have to play to unlock the answers. Split into six sections, once you complete each one, it unveils one digit of a six-digit code that you can crack to unlock files and 'access The Capitol vault'. It's simple, but once you get sucked in, you'll find it's quite addictive.

Industry observers note that starting off simple and easy, Google tests your Hunger Games literacy with questions such as 'Who remarked "I volunteer as tribute"?', which you have to unlock by completing a memory game. It seems like a breeze at first; you're also asked questions about other characters, but then it really tests your Panem knowledge — I can't lie, I started to sweat a little.

Industry observers note that as you complete each quest, the tasks and questions get progressively more challenging to the point where you're quizzed on each District's specialty trade, which, if you've read the books back-to-front, should be a piece of cake. For someone who hasn't read the books (me), this part takes some time to complete.

According to recent reports, luckily, these rounds are quite lenient, eliminating the options you get wrong until you find the correct answer. Although that does mean you have to keep track of which District matches which trade. I played them multiple times, and I still can't remember if District 3 is technology or fishing.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

It has been revealed that once you've completed every quest, you unlock access to a video that stars one of the actors from the upcoming movie, along with one final clue to complete the final puzzle. However, each outcome is different for each player, but when you combine the final clues, it forms the phrase 'the snow may fall, but the sun also rises'.

Type this into the Google search bar, and you'll be taken through to an exclusive, unlisted YouTube video with additional trailer footage from the movie, marking the end of Google's Hunger Games scavenger hunt.

Google's Hunger Games search engine quest is still live, but it's likely to disappear when the movie is released on November 20.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • One of my favorite exercise-tracking apps got even better today with an enhancement that expands its functionality beyond workouts and fitness metrics to better reflect how people actually feel.
  • Starting today, Gentler Streak will let users log how they feel each day, including their mood, symptoms, and other factors that may not be reflected in their health and fitness data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In an update rolling out today, Gentler Streak is introducing upcoming ways for users to track their wellbeing and personalize the app’s guidance based on how they feel. Here are the details.

One of my favorite exercise-tracking apps got even better today with an enhancement that expands its functionality beyond workouts and fitness metrics to better reflect how people actually feel.

Starting today, Gentler Streak will let users log how they feel each day, including their mood, symptoms, and other factors that may not be reflected in their health and fitness data.

In a recent development, some days, the way we feel isn’t reflected in what the data says, no matter the data quality. “How I Feel” captures the part that devices can’t grasp: personal context. And how you feel is not only a mood: it is also a sore throat, heavy legs or a poor night’s sleep. The feature was inspired by the Gentler Streak community, including people living with chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, ADHD, and those not wearing their Apple Watch at night. Without overnight signals, their guidance has less to work with.

According to the team behind Gentler Streak, these new features are aimed at owners whose health and fitness data may not accurately reflect how they feel, including those dealing with chronic conditions, menopause, stress, or poor sleep.

In practice, the app will now feature four tabs: Today, Health, Workouts, and Insights. In the Today and Health tabs, a new “Anything to add?” field will let owners rate how they feel, from Great to Off, and add context about what might be affecting their well-being, including fatigue, feeling calm, or custom tags.

According to recent reports, you decide when the prompt appears. Go to Profile > Settings > Self-Evaluation Prompt and choose one of three options: only when your vitals or sleep are off, always on, or never.

Gentler Stories notes that the self-assessments will override the app’s wellbeing estimates for that day, with its daily guidance adjusting accordingly.

The Today tab will also feature an expanded 10- or 30-day timeline showing logged workouts, wellbeing estimates, potential symptoms, poor sleep or vitals, and the first day of a menstrual period, while Health will introduce an interactive chart showing users how their wellbeing changes over time, with the ability to filter by symptoms.

Customers can now also customize which information appears on their Today screen, including vitals, sleep, steps, menstrual cycle, VO₂ max, and workouts, which is a nice touch.

For owners who are sick, injured, or taking a break from exercise, the app’s hallmark Activity Path will make way for a new Wellbeing Path, which lets them track their wellbeing on a daily basis.

According to recent reports, for consumers with Active status, a latest colorful wellbeing line will appear beneath the Activity Path, reflecting how they feel each day. This information is logged automatically for those who wear their Apple Watch overnight, or based on self-assessments for those who don’t.

Importantly, Gentler Stories notes that all information entered through the fresh feature remains on the user’s device, with no accounts or company-operated servers involved.

Gentler Streak is available for free on the App Store, with in-app purchases for monthly, yearly, family, and lifetime subscriptions.

  • The chip giant, which spent most of the year as the world's most valuable organization, has lost 30% of its value during the losing streak.
  • Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and led it for 33 years, resigned on Thursday after two separate extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and the other with an employee — were made public.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia investors turned bearish before this week's Jensen Huang saga. But the selling on Wall Street accelerated in the past few days, sending the stock to its sixth straight weekly drop, the longest losing streak since 2012.

The chip giant, which spent most of the year as the world's most valuable organization, has lost 30% of its value during the losing streak. That's a drop of roughly $1.7 trillion in market cap and it pushed the company below Apple.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and led it for 33 years, resigned on Thursday after two separate extramarital affairs — one with an alleged Chinese spy and the other with an employee — were made public. The board named finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO while it conducts a search for a full-time successor.

It has been revealed that nvidia shares fell 13% this week, the most since April 2025. News of the first reported affair hit the front pages over the weekend, when Huang sent a letter to employees apologizing for being "unfaithful to my wife." The board convened late Wednesday after The Upcoming York Times reported on the other affair, this one with the manufacturer's vice president of health care.

By early Thursday morning, Huang was out, capping a stunning fall for the Nvidia co-founder, who had emerged as one of President Donald Trump's top allies in the corporate world.

"With the unfortunate departure of CEO Jensen Huang we expect a challenging transition for NVIDIA over the next few months," Gil Luria, an analyst at D.A. Davidson, wrote in a report on Thursday. Luria lowered his price target to $200 from $300, but maintained his buy rating. "We believe the market has appropriately adjusted for this transition," he wrote.

Sources indicate that last week, prior to Huang's departure, Nvidia shares dropped about 9%. Much of the decline came after the midterm elections, which resulted in sweeping victories for Democrats and the passage of dozens of ballot measures that could slow the artificial intelligence buildout.

In the weeks before the election, Nvidia's stock was sliding alongside the rest of the AI trade on concerns that rising interest rates would punish debt-heavy companies. While Nvidia is wildly profitable, big customers like neoclouds are reliant on the debt markets.

It has been revealed that heading into next week, the pressure is on Kress. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Tuesday. Analysts are projecting 91% year-over-year revenue growth to $108.9 billion, according to LSEG. That's up 18-fold from the same quarter in 2022, just before OpenAI rolled out ChatGPT and kicked off the generative AI era.

Analysts at Oppenheimer wrote in a report on Thursday that, even though they see the company reporting solid earnings, "we expect fundamentals to take a backseat near term.".

"The departure of Mr. Huang could, in our view, translate to a lingering share overhang," they wrote.

Recent findings suggest that max. 24 hours(ANC ON), Max. 32 hours(ANC OFF).

USB-C, 3.5 hrs for full charge; 5 min charging for up to 1.5 hrs playtime.

10-band EQ (app), DSEE Ultimate AI upscaling.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve reviewed luxury headphones from Bowers & Wilkins, Noble Audio, FiiO, Dali, and others, and the 1000X The Collexion feels every bit as luxurious. While the 1000XM6 headphones are very comfortable, I have a huge melon, and the earcups can feel a bit too cozy after long periods of wear.

Industry observers note that that’s no longer the case with 1000X The Collexion (1000X going forward). They are beautifully crafted, from the yokes to the accents. Though they no longer fold into a “ball” like the XM6, their case is only slightly larger.

Recent findings suggest that the cans glide on upcoming metal arms with ease and look every bit the high price you’re going to pay for them. The metal, soft faux leather, and soft-touch materials create a tactile experience unlike what the XM6 offers. The 1000X feels hefty, substantial, but not heavy on my head at all.

In a recent development, the earcups are deeper and softer than the XM6, and though those have plenty of vertical travel to adjust to the right fit for you, the 1000X just feels more premium in its glide and fit. They kept the springs that let them tilt so they sit firmly against your head, but the clamping force never felt fatiguing for me. Not even after hours-long listening sessions.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

The oversized silver grommets around the ports and silver buttons give the headphones an industrial-art aesthetic that complements the mirror-polished yokes. During my testing period, I found the 1000X more comfortable than the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2, which cost $150 more. That's largely because of the generous earcups and their soft faux leather.

All of the embellishments and comfort should be expected, though, at $650 for this limited-edition pair of active noise-canceling headphones that you can pick up directly from Sony or at various online and brick-and-mortar retailers.

I listened to my test playlists, utilizing Bluetooth 6.0 with both the LDAC and LE Audio codecs, connected to a Google Pixel 11.

Recent findings suggest that I also connected via wire to the FiiO M21 DAP and listened to Hi-Res audio and MP3 audio to test the DSEE Ultimate. During my testing, I compared them to the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2, Sennheiser HDB 630, and the Sony WH-1000XM6 over-ear headphones, with some interesting results.

According to recent reports, the venerable WH-1000XM6 sits atop many people’s lists for its sound quality and its active noise canceling, but Sony has taken sound quality even further. Let’s talk about ANC first, though, because what you get with the 1000X ultimately comes from the decision to upgrade the sound quality.

According to recent reports, when it comes to top-tier over-ear wireless headphones, there are generally two camps: those that prioritize ANC potency over audio quality, and those that prioritize audio quality over ANC. For the former, we’re talking about Sony, Bose, and Apple. For the latter, we’re talking about Sennheiser, Bowers & Wilkins, Noble, Dali, and Focal.

Recent findings suggest that so, how does Sony do with its everyday-use XM6 against the luxury 1000X? ANC efficacy across the frequency spectrum is better with the XM6. You’re getting better mid- and high-frequency performance out of the XM6, and that’s because sound quality is prioritized with the 1000X.

In a recent development, that said, most people who do a 1-to-1 test between the two and their ANC strength probably won’t notice a significant difference. The difference I did notice was an audible improvement in soundstage size with the 1000X with ANC on. While ANC may be slightly weaker with the 1000X, they’re more open.

They have a noticeably larger soundstage where the airy feeling of Lady Blacksmith Mombaza’s intro on Paul Simon’s “Diamonds on the Souls of Her Shoes” feels like you’re listening to it at the Hollywood Bowl. Jazz arrangements like that on Thelonious Monk’s “Monk’s Dream (Take 8)” sound more like live productions than the somewhat constricted headspace you get with the XM6.

Recent findings suggest that my only complaint with the stock sound of the 1000X is that it’s missing a bit of sparkle, like what you get with the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2. Listening to those, music really comes alive and feels live, like you’re sitting next to the musician. The Px8 S2 also excels with microdetails, though the 1000X has very good detail retrieval.

In a recent development, the 1000X exceeds the Px8 S2 in bass response, though. The Px8 S2 can’t match the 1000X’s low-frequency rumble and sub-bass reproduction, and if you want to dial that low-end frequency response back a bit, you have more control with Sony’s Sound Connect app’s 10-band EQ. Bowers & Wilkins gives you only five bands.

The next-best option is the Sennheiser HDB 630, which has a stock EQ and bass response very similar to the 1000X, but you get even greater sound-shaping control with Sennheiser’s parametric EQ. What you don’t get with the large HDB 630 is the same level of ANC as the 1000X or the same portability, since the HDB 630 has a larger case and feels bulkier.

In a recent development, sony’s Sound Connect app is very well done. It’s well laid out, easy to customize, and gives you plenty of options to tailor the headphones' listening, calling, and ANC experiences.

Sources indicate that I really like the case, too. It is a bit large, but I like the styling, with the built-in handle. That detail feels like a luxury upgrade over the XM6. As much as I do like the Platinum color that I have for review, if I were buying, I’d go with black. I can see the soft-touch surface on the earcups becoming problematic with smudges.

These don’t have enough clamping force to wear to the gym. Also, for $650, I’d avoid getting them sweaty. If I need tunes to propel me through workouts, I’d worry a lot less about gym-centric headphones like Apple’s Beats 360.

You can listen to them via a wired connection, which I don’t think many will take the time to do. You should, though, because that opens up a whole world of lossless audio options. Given that these are more for static passive and active listening sessions, wired listening could be a “no-brainer.” Just keep in mind that they support wired via a 3.5mm cable, not USB-C.

Like a spa treatment for your ears.

It has been revealed that the Sony 1000X The Collexion is one of the most comfortable over-ear ANC headphones I've reviewed to date. Add very strong ANC, solid detail retrieval and clarity, and excellent app-based customization options, and you have a solid contender in the luxury headphone market.
